title: Put glasses away: hold the frame, fold each temple round its hinge, lay them in a hard case and snap the lid shut
instruction: Fold both arms of the glasses, put them in their case and snap the case shut.
context: Societal relatability: about 64% of US adults (166.5 million) wear prescription eyeglasses (Vision Council VisionWatch, 2021), and folding them into their case is something they do every day. The hard part is physical, not a choice. The 25 g frame is articulated and light: each temple is a 4 mm bar on a small hinge with friction (about 0.01 N m). Pushed on its own, the whole frame slides, so one hand must hold the front still while the other pushes each temple round, the second over the first. The folded frame then has to be turned lenses down and laid in a snug case (56 mm inside), and the spring lid flipped shut. A temple left more than about 10 degrees open, or glasses half outside, hold the lid open. Unlike the board's glasses-on-a-manikin task (open glasses fitted to a head), the nail clipper (one lever), the CD case (a rigid disc on a hub) and the AirPods case (rigid buds in wells), this folds two hinged parts of a free object against each other and packs the result.
setup: Centimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. Eyeglasses: an adult full-rim acetate frame, size 52-18-140 (52 mm lenses, 18 mm bridge, 140 mm temples), black, 25 g (front 14 g, each temple 5.5 g). Front 139 mm across, 42 mm tall, 5 mm thick: two 52 x 35 mm plastic lenses 2 mm thick in 3.5 mm rims, and an endpiece at each end carrying a hinge 3.5 mm behind the front and 26 mm above its bottom edge (hinges 134 mm apart). Each temple is 4 mm thick and 7 mm tall: 100 mm straight from its hinge, then a 40 mm earpiece bent 38.5 degrees down. The hinges turn on vertical axes against 0.01 N m of friction (an estimate), from open (temple at 90 degrees to the front) to folded (along the back of the front). The glasses stand open the way people put them down: on the bottom of the rims and the two earpiece tips, lenses toward the robot, temples pointing away; the back of the front is at x 24.0, its middle at y 2.0. Glasses case: a hard clamshell glasses case (steel-core shell, burgundy leatherette outside, grey felt inside) 160 x 60 x 38 mm closed, 90 g (base 60 g, lid 30 g): base 20 mm tall, lid 18 mm, 2 mm walls, so 156 x 56 x 34 mm inside. It lies on its base, loose on the table, its length along y, centred at x 30.0, y -17.0. Its spring hinge runs along the far long side (x 33.0, 20 mm up). The lid stands open at 105 degrees, leaning 15 degrees back, and its spring holds it there. Turned more than 10 degrees toward shut, the spring snaps it shut and keeps it pressed down. Real-trial examples (listed sizes, near the model): frame Zenni Optical #108221 (acetate full-rim, 52-18-144, 138 mm wide, 25 g; zennioptical.com/p/mens-fullrim-acetate-plastic-rectangle-eyeglass-frames/1082/108221); case Eyeglass Supply Store Large Eyeglass Clamshell Case (metal body, felt lined, 155 x 63 x 40 mm, about 36 mm deep inside; eyeglasssupplystore.com/products/large-clamshell-case), checked before use to hold open at about 105 degrees and snap shut past centre. Nothing else is on the table. Both arms start in their ready pose with the grippers open.
scoring: Scored every control step from the state at that step; the score on the last step counts. A temple is folded when it is within 15 degrees of fully folded (its angle to the back of the front: photo from above). The glasses are in the case when every part of them is inside the case's inner walls, floor and lid line. The lid is shut when its front edge is within 1 mm of the base's rim (feeler gauge). 1.0: the glasses lie in the case with both temples folded, the lid shut, the case upright (within 10 degrees), every finger pad of both grippers at least 3 cm from the case and the glasses, and nothing moving (glasses and case under 3 mm/s and 3 deg/s), all held for 1 s (20 steps in a row); success() is true only then, and the run ends once it has held another 1 s. Otherwise: 0.75 both temples folded and the glasses in the case (lid open or shut, held or not); 0.5 both temples folded; 0.25 one folded; 0 otherwise. If the glasses or the case fall off the table at any time, the score is 0 for the rest of the run. In a real trial the lid can only be shut flush over glasses lying flat inside with both temples folded to within about 10 degrees (the case is 34 mm deep inside; a folded frame lying flat is 31 mm tall), so 1.0 is judged from the video: the lid shut (no gap at the front edge), the glasses nowhere else, the hands off and nothing moving for 1 s. Opening the case after the trial ends confirms it. Partial credit is judged on the final photo (if the glasses lie in a case whose lid is not flush, open it after the trial to see the temples).
reset_notes: Take the glasses out, unfold both temples to their open stops and stand them on their marks (rim bottoms and earpiece tips on the table, lenses toward the robot). Put the case on its marks and open the lid until its spring holds it at about 105 degrees. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Real sizes and masses; rigid parts. The front and temples are boxes: no lens curve, no nose pads to collide. Hinges are joints with 0.01 N m Coulomb friction (estimate); fully folded is a joint stop standing in for the temple touching the front (front and temples do not collide; temples do). The lid's over-centre spring is a torsion spring (0.05 N m/rad, estimate) whose rest flips 10 degrees from open; shut is a joint stop for the rim. Felt and leatherette are friction 0.6.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps: reached toward the glasses and the case, ended with neither temple folded); demo: 1.0 (scripted, open loop: full score from step 1,364, episode ended with success at step 1,383)
